set_aside.subject: Audit action to entity reference mapping
set_aside.text: “The use case that owns a significant action builds its AuditIntent” while audit_writer owns “validation of an AuditIntent” and A23 requires entity_id to identify “the audited entity”; no text maps each AuditAction to its required entity_kind and entity_id.
set_aside.question: Which module owns the action-to-entity mapping, and what entity_kind/entity_id must each audit action carry so audit_writer can validate it without knowing business modules or repositories?
options: The owning use case chooses the affected entity and audit_writer validates only generic shape and canonical UUID syntax.
audit_writer owns a closed AuditAction-to-AuditEntityKind mapping, while the caller supplies the identifier.
audit_writer receives additional trusted entity evidence enabling it to verify both kind and identifier.
set_aside.default_guess: Give audit_writer a closed action-to-entity-kind table and require each owning use case to supply that entity's canonical identifier.

witness.initial: An active viewer V exists and an administrator issues a new ViewerAccessCredential C for V.
events: viewer_access creates C and builds the viewer.credential_issue AuditIntent.
audit_writer validates and appends the record.
outcomes: The record uses entity_kind=viewer_credential and entity_id=C because the newly issued credential is the affected entity.
The record uses entity_kind=viewer and entity_id=V because credential issuance is an action on the viewer's access lifecycle.
witness.observer: An administrator or auditor reading the audit trail sees a different referenced entity and follows a different record.

set_aside.subject: Actor provenance for staff.login_failed
set_aside.text: “staff.login_failed” must write a rejected audit record, but AuditIntent requires actor_id for actor_kind=staff and permits no actor_id only for actor_kind=system; the texts do not say how an unauthenticated or nonexistent login identity is represented.
set_aside.question: What actor_kind and actor_id must audit_writer accept for staff.login_failed when authentication did not establish a StaffAccount, and must known-account and unknown-account failures use the same representation?
options: Always record actor_kind=system with actor_id absent.
Use actor_kind=staff with the stored staff_id when the normalized email exists, and system with no actor for an unknown email.
Do not write staff.login_failed when no StaffAccount can be identified.
set_aside.default_guess: Always use actor_kind=system with no actor_id, because a failed login has not authenticated a staff principal.

events: A caller submits that email and a password to staff login.
staff_identity performs the existence-hiding failure path and asks audit_writer to record staff.login_failed.
outcomes: audit_writer accepts a system actor with no actor_id and one login-failure record is stored.
The operation cannot construct a valid staff actor, so no record is stored or AuditIntent validation fails.
witness.observer: An operator inspecting audit records or operational failures sees either a recorded failed attempt or an absent/failed audit.
